title: Private Deployments - VPC & On-Prem Reference Architectures, Packaging, Day-2 Ops, Upgrades & Customer Requirements Library
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended reference architectures, packaging guidance, day-2 operations runbooks, upgrade & rollback procedures, and the customer requirements library for private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for Solutions Engineers, SREs, and Customer Engineering teams who run or support customer private deployments.

Goals
- Provide a single operational reference covering architecture, packaging, and operational procedures.
- Reduce onboarding friction for new customers and shorten time-to-first-query.
- Minimize risk during upgrades and day-2 operations by standardizing checklists and fallbacks.

Ownership and Scope
- Owner: eng-private-deployments (Customer Engineering & Platform SRE collaboration)
- Primary contacts: Asha Patel (Technical Lead), Liam Chen (SRE), Sofia Martinez (Packaging)
- Scope: VPC-hosted private control plane and on-prem air-gapped deployments with Redwood runtime and packaging options.

Reference Architectures (summary)
1) VPC-hosted private control plane + customer-managed compute (recommended for most enterprise customers)
  - Control plane: Redwood managed in a customer-dedicated VPC peering or PrivateLink (option).
  - Compute: customer-owned GPU nodes in private subnets (Kubernetes or VM fleet).
  - Network: Transit gateway or VPC peering for cross-account access; enforce NACLs and security groups with whitelisting for control plane endpoints.
  - Storage: S3-compatible object storage (in-region) for model artifacts; encrypted at rest with customer KMS.
  - Identity: SAML/SCIM for user provisioning; mTLS for node-to-control-plane RPC.

2) Fully on-prem, air-gapped deployment (regulated/isolated environments)
  - Control plane can be deployed as a customer-managed private control plane with optional offline license verification.
  - Packaging: OCI images plus offline tarballs for images and Debian packages for bootstrapping.
  - Hardware: recommended GPU families (A100 80GB, H100 variants) and rack-level network (100GbE).
  - Storage: local NVMe for model cache + network-attached object store (if available) or Redwood-provided object store appliance.

3) Hybrid: Dedicated compute inside customer cloud with on-prem enclave for sensitive data processing
  - Useful when customers require low-latency local inference with central management.
  - Use secure routing, token exchange, and transparent model pinning.

High-level component list
- Redwood runtime (containerized)
- Control plane (private)
- Model artifact store (S3 compatible)
- Inference pool (Kubernetes DaemonSets or managed VM cluster)
- Monitoring and logging stack (Prometheus, Loki, Grafana or equivalents)
- KMS/HSM integrations
- Audit logging sink (SIEM-compatible)

Packaging and Distribution
- On-prem packaging options:
  1) Full OCI registry bundle (preferred): customers run a local registry and we push verified images via a secure pipeline or provide offline bundle.
  2) Offline tarball + installer: for air-gapped sites; includes images, Helm charts, and a signed manifest.
  3) Appliance image: pre-baked VM image (OVA) for small-footprint or demo installs.
- Packaging checklist:
  - Signed image manifest with SHA256 for all artifacts.
  - Included preflight script (checks disk, kernel modules, NVidia driver versions, available GPUs).
  - Installer idempotency (re-runnable).
  - Post-install verification steps and smoke tests (sample inference request, metrics emission).

Minimum supported platform requirements (summary table)
| Component | Minimum | Recommended | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| GPU | 1x A100-40GB | 4x A100-80GB / H100 | For production: multi-GPU per worker to support batching |
| RAM (per host) | 64 GB | 256 GB | Large models and KV cache require ample RAM |
| Disk | 500 GB SSD | 2 TB NVMe | Model cache + local logs |
| Network | 10 GbE | 100 GbE | RDMA recommended for multi-node KV sync |

Customer Requirements Library (categorization)
- Security & Compliance
  - SAML 2.0 + SCIM provisioning support
  - Customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, Vault/HSM)
  - Audit log forwarding (syslog/S3/Splunk)
- Networking
  - VPC peering or PrivateLink support
  - Explicit CIDR ranges and approved egress endpoints list
  - Proxy/HTTP(S) egress configuration for images and control-plane metadata
- Hardware & Capacity
  - Supported GPU SKUs and driver versions
  - Minimum capacity and headroom requirements for autoscaling policies
- Operational
  - Backup windows and retention (model artifacts)
  - RPO/RTO expectations for control plane and inference pools
  - Maintenance window SLA and out-of-hours support expectations

Day-2 Operations and Runbooks (key procedures)
1) Onboarding checklist (high level)
  1. Confirm customer environment and baseline (network, quotas, hardware).
  2. Exchange manifests and image access (registry or offline bundle).
  3. Run preflight verifier on every node.
  4. Perform staging deployment and run smoke tests.
  5. Cutover and validate traffic routing, metrics, and logging.

2) Routine day-2 tasks
  - Model deployment: validate model artifacts (SHA256), update model catalog, perform canary rollout 5% -> 25% -> 100% with evaluation prompts.
  - Node reprovision: gracefully drain node, evacuate KV cache, reinstall drivers if needed, rejoin cluster.
  - Capacity scaling: run autoscaling policy test (scale-up and scale-down), validate queueing/backpressure behavior.
  - Backup verification: periodic restore test of model artifacts.

3) Incident triage quick-start
  - Severity classification: P0/P1/P2 mapping to customer impact.
  - Immediate actions: confirm SLO impact (latency >250ms p95 or error rate >5%), engage oncall SRE, gather logs and metrics (control-plane, runtime, GPU health).
  - Mitigations: fallback to smaller model variant, divert traffic to dedicated spare pool, or enable cached response mode.
  - Post-incident: run postmortem template and update runbook.

Upgrade and Rollback Procedures
- Principles:
  - Always run upgrades first in staging, then canary, then full production.
  - Use automated health checks and traffic shifting during rollout.
  - Preserve model artifact compatibility and KV cache migrations must be reversible.

Typical upgrade workflow (numbered procedure)
1. Prepare release bundle and run automated integration tests in CI.
2. Notify stakeholders and schedule maintenance window per customer SLA.
3. Snapshot control-plane DB and back up model store.
4. Deploy control-plane patch to canary customer cluster (1 node or 5% traffic).
5. Monitor health (30-60 minutes): metrics to watch: control-plane errors, API latency, model load failures, GPU temperature and memory faults.
6. If canary passes, roll out to 25% -> 50% -> 100% using automated traffic shifting (5-15 minute intervals).
7. Post-upgrade verification: run evaluation prompt set, check cost/latency baselines, validate audit logs and KMS access.
8. If regression observed, immediately trigger rollback:
  - Rollback steps:
    a) Shift traffic away from upgraded nodes to previous revision (traffic-split or feature-flag).
    b) Redeploy prior control-plane image and restore DB snapshot if migration caused incompatibility.
    c) Verify KV cache compatibility or flush caches and rebuild.
    d) Open incident and notify customer with RCA timeline.

Rollback criteria (examples)
- p95 latency regression > 20% vs baseline for more than 10 mins
- Error rate increase > 2% absolute and >50% relative for core inference APIs
- Model degradation on evaluation suite (drop in pass rate >= 5%)

Preflight and Smoke Test examples
- Preflight (bash):
  #!/bin/bash
  set -e
  echo "Checking GPU driver"
  nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,memory.total --format=csv || exit 1
  echo "Checking docker"
  docker --version || exit 1
  echo "Checking curl to control plane"
  curl -sSf https://control-plane.example.local/healthz || exit 1
  echo "Preflight OK"

- Smoke test (curl):
  curl -sS -X POST https://local-runtime.example.local/v1/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"input":"Hello world"}' | jq .

Monitoring and SLOs (recommended)
- SLOs
  - Control plane: availability 99.95% monthly
  - Inference API: p99 latency < 600ms for short-form generation; custom SLOs per customer
  - Model load success: 99.9%
- Alerts (examples)
  - Control-plane unhealthy endpoints > 3 nodes for 5 minutes
  - GPU ECC errors > 1/hour
  - Model load failures >= 1% of requests over 15 minutes

Security and Compliance Considerations
- KMS integration: recommend customer-managed keys and strict key rotation policies.
- Network policies: default-deny with explicit egress allowlist for control plane endpoints and image registries.
- Audit logging: stream events to customer SIEM and keep tamper-evident logs for at least 90 days.

Templates and Artifacts (links and command examples)
- Helm charts: packaged under artifacts/redwood-helm/<version>
- Offline bundle layout:
  /bundle/
    - images/ (OCI tarballs)
    - charts/ (Helm charts)
    - manifests/ (signed manifest.json)
    - preflight.sh
  - installers/ (installer binary)

Troubleshooting matrix (common issues)
- Symptom: model fails to load
  - Likely causes: manifest mismatch, insufficient GPU memory, incompatible weights
  - Steps: check model artifact SHA256, check runtime logs (/var/log/redwood/runtime.log), validate GPU memory via nvidia-smi
- Symptom: high latency p95
  - Likely causes: noisy neighbor, insufficient batching, network egress throttling
  - Steps: validate node-level metrics, temporarily route traffic to spare pool, increase batch window if appropriate

Frequently asked questions
- Q: Can customers run mixed-precision quantized models on customer GPUs?
  - A: Yes, we provide quantization profiles and recommend H100/A100 series; ensure CUDA and NCCL versions listed in the preflight.
- Q: How are software licenses managed for offline installs?
  - A: We issue time-bound signed license tokens and support periodic offline revalidation during maintenance windows.

Appendix: Useful commands and sample configs
- List pods (K8s): kubectl -n redwood get pods -o wide
- Drain node: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- Sample model manifest (YAML snippet):
  model:
    id: "redwood-v1-7b"
    sha256: "abc123..."
    signature: "MEUCIQ..."
